To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the first finger of human TR is stabilized by a series of H--bond and that the complex of the first finger with hexanucleotidic duplex from TRE is stabilized by a network of H-bonds between the side chains of finger and the base pairs of the duplex.

the finger is stabilized by a series of H-bonds (5 in the backbone, 2 on the side chains, and 2 between the backbone and side chains) and the complex is stabilized by hydrogen bonding between the side chains of Tyr11, His12, Tyr13, and Arg14 and bases G2, G8, and G3.
(a) Thyroid hormone receptor (TR) is a member of the steroid/thyroid superfamily of nuclear receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the structure and dynamics of proteins, nucleic acids, and complexes thereof.
the study of interaction between thyroid hormone receptor (TR) and DNA by molecular mechanics simulation techniques.
the study of the molecular mechanism of DNA binding by zinc finger proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interaction of the finger with DNA involves a combination of H-bonding and van der Waals interactions.
the finger binds to DNA by H-bonding to the bases and by stacking with the base pair.
the finger interacts with the hexanucleotide DNA by H-bonding, stacking and conformational change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our results are in good agreement with the crystallographic data and the results of the molecular dynamics simulation.
the interaction of the finger with DNA is mainly due to H--bonding between side chain of finger and bases and backbone of DNA.
our results support the view that the zinc finger from thyroid hormone receptor interacts with DNA through a combination of direct contacts and protein-induced changes in DNA conformation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interaction of finger with DNA is mainly electrostatic in nature and is stabilized by H--bonds between side chains and DNA.
the DNA is not a simple passive partner in the complex formation, rather the complex formation is a dynamic process.
it is possible to use the molecular mechanics simulation technique to predict the structure of protein--DNA complex.
